chunks: From him, from Ibn Ribat, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to [selling] one garment for two garments."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell one piece of clothing for two pieces of clothing in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on sales, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) via the chain of Zurarah clarifies that exchanging one garment for two is permissible (*lā ba'sa*), addressing the specific juristic concern of *gharar* (uncertainty) in barter. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh as it distinguishes between simple barter (*mubada'a*) and sales (*bay'*), often interpreted to mean that such an exchange is valid provided the items are of the same genus (e.g., both are woolen garments) to avoid the prohibition of selling a debt for a debt or uncertainty in quantity/quality.
